newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche diagnoses dilution in Boehringer buy.
newsitem.headline: Roche diagnoses dilution in Boehringer buy.

text.p: Roche Holding AG expects to suffer a little pain through temporary earnings dilution in its $11 blllion acquisition of diagnostics firm Boehringer Mannheim Group.
The purchase of the German drugs group, whose parent is Bermuda-based Corange Ltd, will if approved make Roche world leader in the fast-growing medical diagnostics business, Roche said.

Roche executives said that some earnings dilution in the first year of the acquisition would be unavoidable, due to the cost of the deal and the fact that Roche will have to bankroll some high-yielding liquid investments to pay for it.

In a news briefing following the acquistion announcement, Roche chief financial officer Henri Meier said that the method of financing the transaction will depend to a large degree on the timing of the takeover, and the conditions in financial markets at that time.
"We will probably take a bridging loan," Meier said, adding today's nominally low interest rates make such a credit attractive. Meier also said the dilution will be "quite significant."
"And it will take some time until we are back at the same level of profitability," Meier said.

Speaking at a news briefing following Monday's announcement, company executives said the newly combined unit, Roche Boehringer Mannheim Diagnostics, would have a market share of an estimated between 11 and 15 percent, depending upon which exchange rate is used.

"This acquisition enables Roche to attain yet another of its strategic goals, to become a leader in the diagnostics systems and products sector in terms of sales and profitability," Fritz Gerber, chairman of Roche's executive committee and board, said in a statement.
The decision won rare praise from Roche competitor Novartis AG.

"It is a good move for Roche. It make a lot of sense, especially for the diagnostic part of their business," Daniel Vasella, chief executive of Novartis, told reporters at the International Managaement Symposium in St Gallen.
The news also pushed Roche shares to a new year high.
Roche's bearer shares peaked at 20,100 before pulling back in late afternoon to 19,880, still up 485 Swiss francs.
The deal also involves taking Corange's 84.2 percent of DePuy Inc, a Delware-based manufacturer of orthopedic products.
Roche said it has no plans to sell Delaware-based DePuy.
"I think there is a significant growth market there," said Fritz Gerber, chairman of Roche's executive committee and board, refering to DePuy.
Gerber said "no" when asked if DePuy was up for sale.

Roche also said the move would not result in delays of goals set at the start of 1997, particularly the launch of its cardiovascular agent Posicor, anti-obesity drug Xenical and Parkinson's disease treatment Tasmar.
Markus Rausch, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Frankfurt said the merger had been rumoured for some time and made sense.
The planned deal will also heighten competition in the diagnostics business, especially for German pharmaceutical firms Hoechst and Bayer AG, analysts said.
The consolidation could push some smaller players out of the market, analysts said.
-- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
